definition: LinkedIn is an online professional network for maintaining career profiles, connecting with contacts, and discovering jobs or professional content.
example: A recruiter posts a vacancy and reviews profiles of people interested in the role.

definition: Linux systems administration involves operating and maintaining Linux hosts, including users, packages, storage, services and monitoring.
example: An administrator updates packages on a host and verifies that its scheduled services still run.

definition: Liquidity forecasting estimates when funds become available and when payments are due to anticipate cash shortfalls or surpluses.
example: A treasury team forecasts whether upcoming payroll will require a short-term transfer.

definition: Listwise deletion removes an entire observation from an analysis when any required variable is missing for that observation.
example: A regression omits survey responses missing either the outcome or a selected predictor.

definition: LiveData is an Android Jetpack observable data holder that delivers updates with awareness of an observer's lifecycle.
example: An Android screen observes a view model's LiveData to display changes when the screen is active.

definition: Livestreaming transmits audio, video or both to viewers with only a short delay while the event takes place.
example: A producer streams a conference talk and monitors audio and video quality during the broadcast.

definition: LLM observability is the practice of collecting and inspecting signals about a language-model application's execution and output quality.
example: An engineer uses traces to see whether slow answers originate in retrieval or model generation.

definition: Load securement is the process of restraining transported cargo to prevent shifting or loss during transit.
example: A driver checks that approved restraints hold the pallets in place before departure.

definition: Loan administration manages the records, disbursements, payments, notices and servicing requirements of approved loans.
example: A servicing team reconciles received payments with the balances in its loan records.

definition: Loan structuring designs financing terms such as amount, maturity, repayment schedule, collateral and covenants to fit the transaction's needs and risks.
example: A lender proposes seasonal payment dates based on the borrower's cash flow.

definition: Loan syndication arranges financing in which several lenders participate under coordinated terms for one borrower.
example: A lead bank organizes a group of lenders to share a loan larger than any wants to hold alone.

definition: Log management collects, stores, organizes and evaluates records of events from systems and applications.
example: An operations team searches centralized logs to determine which service first reported an outage.

definition: Logic diagrams represent logical relationships or decision conditions using symbols and connections.
example: An engineer diagrams how two input signals determine an interlock status.
sense_note: May refer to circuit logic or formal decision diagrams, depending on context.

definition: Logistics planning coordinates how goods and materials are stored, transported and delivered within time, capacity and cost constraints.
example: A distributor combines small shipments into routes that meet delivery windows.

definition: Logo design creates a distinctive visual mark that represents an organization, product or brand.
example: A designer checks that a new mark remains recognizable on both an app icon and a printed sign.

definition: Long short-term memory is a recurrent neural network architecture that uses gates to retain, update or discard information across sequence steps.
example: A model uses an LSTM to incorporate earlier measurements while forecasting demand.

definition: A low-code development platform enables applications or workflows to be assembled using visual tools, reusable components and limited custom code.
example: A business team uses a visual builder to create a request form and approval process.

definition: Low-risk neonatal nursing provides routine assessment, monitoring and care for newborns who do not require intensive or high-acuity care.
example: A nurse monitors feeding, temperature and weight in a healthy newborn transition setting.

definition: Low-voltage transistor-transistor logic defines digital signal-level conventions associated with TTL-compatible operation at reduced supply voltages.
example: A board designer checks that a device's logic-high and logic-low thresholds match its receiving interface.

definition: Luigi is a Python library for organizing batch data workflows as tasks with dependencies and tracked outputs.
example: A pipeline runs a report-generation task only after producing its source dataset.

definition: Lumion is architectural visualization software for turning design models into rendered images, animations and scenes.
example: An architect renders a building model with lighting, landscaping and surrounding context.

definition: Lymphedema management aims to control swelling caused by impaired lymph drainage and preserve function through assessment, ongoing care and appropriate treatment.
example: A trained clinician monitors limb measurements and adjusts a prescribed compression plan.

definition: M2Crypto is a Python library that wraps OpenSSL functions for cryptography and secure communications.
example: A developer uses the library to inspect the metadata of a digital certificate.

definition: Machine learning develops models that improve at a defined task by fitting patterns to data rather than relying solely on explicitly written rules.
example: A team trains a classifier to categorize product reviews by topic.

definition: Machine operation involves setting up, controlling and monitoring equipment to carry out its intended task safely.
example: An operator selects the specified run settings and stops the machine when inspection reveals a fault.

definition: Machine tools are powered machines for cutting, shaping or finishing workpieces through controlled movement.
example: A machinist uses a lathe to turn a cylindrical part to the required diameter.

definition: Macintosh Application Environment was software that allowed compatible classic Macintosh applications to run on certain Unix workstations.
example: A user opens a classic Mac application on a supported workstation through MAE.

definition: macOS is Apple's operating system for Mac computers, providing desktop, system and application services.
example: An administrator configures user access and installs an application on a Mac.

definition: Mail distribution routes incoming or outgoing mail to the appropriate recipients or delivery channels.
example: A mailroom worker delivers sorted envelopes to the correct departments.

definition: Mail processing prepares, checks, sorts or records mail and parcels before distribution or dispatch.
example: A clerk verifies package labels and sorts items by destination.

definition: Malware analysis examines suspected malicious software to understand its behavior, effects and indicators so defenders can detect or contain it.
example: A defender documents files changed by a suspected program in an isolated analysis environment.

definition: Mammalian cell culture maintains or grows mammal-derived cells outside their organism for research or controlled production.
example: A scientist uses cultured mammalian cells to study a cellular response to a candidate treatment.

definition: A manure spreader is farm equipment that applies animal manure to land as a nutrient source or soil amendment.
example: A farmer uses the implement to distribute manure evenly across the area identified in a nutrient plan.

definition: Map production combines geographic data, cartographic design and publishing to create maps for an intended use.
example: A planner produces a printed map that distinguishes flood zones from roads and building footprints.

definition: Map reading interprets a map's symbols, scale, orientation and features to determine locations or relationships.
example: A hiker uses contour lines to identify the steepest part of a planned route.

definition: MapDB is a Java library for collections that can store data on disk or in memory.
example: A Java application keeps a large key-value index on disk using a persistent map.

definition: Marine navigation plans and monitors a vessel's movement using charts, positions, environmental conditions and navigational aids.
example: A watch officer compares the vessel's position with its planned track before entering a channel.

definition: Marine radar detects surrounding vessels, shorelines and other reflecting objects using radio waves.
example: A watch officer checks radar contacts when visibility falls in fog.

definition: Marionette.js is a JavaScript framework that builds on Backbone to organize application views, regions and related interface behavior.
example: A developer divides a dashboard into regions that display and replace their own views.

definition: Maritime law enforcement applies laws and regulations affecting vessels, waters or maritime activity within the agency's jurisdiction.
example: A maritime officer checks a vessel's required safety documentation during an authorized inspection.
